key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves multiscale CFD surrogate reconstruction by combining spectral encoding, PDE-aware attention, and self-supervised pretraining to better recover localized flow structures.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to accelerate real-world fluid simulations while preserving near-body, wake, and far-wake dynamics needed for engineering analysis and design.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow features
Physics-biased self-attention guided by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Across cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best aggregate accuracy, including an all-channel NMSE of 0.05875 and Pearson correlation of 0.97019 on cylinder wake, and NMSE of 2.70×10^-4 on FSI.
watch_item: The approach is benchmarked on two specific real flow cases, so generalization, training cost, and sensitivity to PDE residual quality should be verified before broader deployment.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
